text:
Morgan: quick follow-up to the RFC I posted yesterday — thinking through operator contract for resumable package upgrades in air-gapped installs. link: https://rfc.internal/airgap-resume (short TL;DR below)
Lia: saw it, skimmed. main gap for me is operator UX when we partially apply a delta and then lose physical media. how do we avoid double-apply or corrupt state? :thinking:
Ana: +1. We need idempotent activation markers and a small on-disk journal that survives reboots. operator should be able to reconcile using a manifest + merkle root of applied blobs.
Sandeep: can we avoid an on-disk DB? many customer nodes are low IO. maybe a compact marker file with tuple: (manifest-hash, activation-window, applied-blob-ids).
Morgan: yeah that's the idea — tiny marker. proposal in RFC: write a sealed "activation-stamp" file to /var/lib/redwood/activation with format:

```
activation_version: 1
manifest_hash: sha256:... 
applied_blobs: ["b3f..", "d1a.."]
state: applying | activated | aborting
```

Lia: if state==applying and operator restarts, it should resume from applied_blobs list. but what about partial blob writes? need write-then-rename atomicity and blob-level checksums.
Kevin: atomic rename + verified SHA on each blob is fine. Also: should operator fence the node to avoid serving new requests until activation finishes? That increases downtime but safer.
Ana: we usually prefer graceful degradation: keep serving on old model until activation==activated, but reject write operations that touch modelstore. sounds fine.
Sandeep: tradeoff: offline media might contain multiple deltas. how do we choose ordering? RFC suggested manifest sequence numbers with dependencies. operator should validate sequence and support reordering if prerequisites missing.
Morgan: yes, manifests will include a small dependency graph and per-blob size and compressed-size hints so operator can estimate disk usage before starting.
Lia: bit worried about disk pressure and rollback safety. What's rollback plan if activation fails after half the blobs applied? do we leave tombstones or attempt roll-forward from a seed image?
Kevin: two options: (1) keep a retained previous-image snapshot and quick symlink flip (fast rollback), or (2) design forward-only roll that uses rebase deltas (requires upstream delta to be present). given air-gapped constraints, snapshot+symlink is safer.
Ana: snapshotting large model files is expensive. instead consider copy-on-write layering (overlayfs) for the modelstore directory: create overlay, apply blobs into upper layer, validate, then switch mount. cheaper than full copy.
Sandeep: overlayfs sounds attractive but not universally available on every distro. we should detect capability and fallback to write-then-rename or require operator to reserve N% free for snapshot.
Morgan: agreed — we'll add a capability probe step to the preflight operator flow. if overlayfs unavailable, fail the upgrade if reservation < X%.
Lia: what about signatures and attestation for offline media? customers need an airgap-compatible signer model. we can't rely on online KMS during install.
Ana: RFC proposed signed manifests + detached signatures that can be verified by a local verifier. for hardware-backed keys, we support HSM/KMS integration when online, but also accept customer-provided trust bundle for offline verification.
Kevin: small nit: include key-ids and signing-algo in manifest header to avoid ambiguous verification.
Morgan: good call. manifest header snippet in RFC (trimmed):

```
{
  "manifest_version": 2,
  "seq": 42,
  "items": [ {"id":"b3f...","sha256":"...","size": 123456}, ... ],
  "signatures": [{"key_id":"pkg-signer-v2","sig":"base64...","algo":"ed25519"}]
}
```

Sandeep: operator should support multiple trust bundles so partner distributions can add their own CAs. also support explicit "accept-once" operator flag for airgap evaluation clusters.
Lia: rollout strategy: we need a canary plan that works offline. RFC idea: local canary flag that marks a subset of nodes to auto-activate while others stay in preflight. operator should expose `--canary-percent` and allow manual promote.
Ana: yep — canary + staged activation. plus builtin telemetry that records activation success/failure to the console (and to S3/ops when online).
Kevin: one more: GC of old blobs. Must avoid accidental GC while some nodes still mid-activation. include an epoch-based retention marker: manifest includes min-retain-until-epoch; operator honors epochs and refuses GC earlier.
Morgan: +1. We'll tie retention epochs to manifest seq and operator heartbeat to the control plane when online. For fully offline, operator uses wallclock + local policy.
Lia: curious about testing — can we add a small harness to simulate media interruption? I can hack something in the operator e2e tests that kills the process mid-blob-write.
Sandeep: please do — that's the best way to validate resume logic. add tests for overlayfs failure paths too.
release-bot: deploy queued: canary agent image v2.3.1 -> test-cluster at 2026-03-24T12:00Z :truck: 
Ana: thanks — sounds like action items: (1) add capability probe and reservation check; (2) add overlayfs fallback doc; (3) embed signature metadata in manifest header; (4) implement activation-stamp and resume path; (5) add e2e interruption tests.
Morgan: I'll update the RFC with these follow-ups and a small reference manifest example. ping me if you want to pair on tests. :pray:
Lia: noted, will add test plan items. thx!
Kevin: I'll draft the snapshot vs overlay FS runtimes and perf notes.
Ana: I'll sketch the offline trust bundle UX for the operator console.
Sandeep: will prototype the reserved-space probe and write a tiny library we can reuse in onprem agent.
Morgan: great — closing the loop. if no objections I'll push the RFC patch later today. :thumbsup:
